promql_issues.issue: sum(rate(service_exceptions_total[5m])) missing by (service) — aggregates globally, masking per-service issues
promql_issues.fix_status: YAML correctly uses sum by (service)(...). Report expression would never fire unless overall exception rate exceeds threshold.

promql_issues.issue: Uses mongo_mem_available_bytes / mongo_mem_total_bytes — metric names don't match YAML convention aws_docdb_freeable_memory_average / aws_docdb_total_memory_average
promql_issues.fix_status: Use aws_docdb_* prefix consistent with CloudWatch exporter.
Use source_matchers / target_matchers per Alertmanager >= 0.22. Existing config already uses correct syntax.

promql_issues.issue: Division-by-zero risk when business_completed_orders_total has zero increase
promql_issues.fix_status: Prometheus returns NaN, which fails > 0.10 comparison, so functionally safe. AND completed > 5 guard already prevents this in practice. No fix needed.

promql_issues.issue: aws_rds_allocated_storage_average — may not be available as a Prometheus metric if using CloudWatch exporter. CloudWatch has AllocatedStorage but it's a static property, not a metric.
promql_issues.fix_status: Verify metric availability. May need to use a recording rule or static label.

promql_issues.issue: Identical condition: both aws_rds_failover_event == 1, for: 0m. Info and Critical fire simultaneously — Info is completely redundant since Critical inhibition (if working) would suppress it.
promql_issues.fix_status: Remove Info tier or differentiate conditions

promql_issues.issue: Uses raw rate() without sum() or sum by (endpoint)(). Evaluates per time series. If endpoint_failures_total has labels like {method, path, status}, the ratio is computed per label combination, potentially giving false positives on low-traffic sub-slices.

rate(...) / container_spec_cpu_quota * container_spec_cpu_period — operator precedence is correct but expression is confusing. Better written as rate(...) * container_spec_cpu_period / container_spec_cpu_quota or use kube_pod_container_resource_limits instead.
delay > 300 OR exceptions > 0 — the OR mixes two different failure modes into one alert. An exception count of 1 in 3 minutes fires as Critical, which may be too aggressive.
promql_issues.fix_status: Consider separating exception alerting from delay alerting

risk_flags.item: RDS ActiveThreads: Flat Thresholds on Heterogeneous Fleet
risk_flags.detail: Flat threshold of 100 is appropriate for Luckin's fleet which is predominantly small instances (t4g/r6g.large). For large instances, ActiveThreads > 100 is still meaningful. Long-term improvement: threads_running / max_connections > 0.30 for Warning, > 0.60 for Critical.
2ms with 5m duration is appropriate. Single-region (us-east-1) minimizes network variance. 10ms Critical threshold provides headroom.

risk_flags.item: BIZ-04 Cancellation Rate: Min 5 Orders Sample Size
risk_flags.detail: Min-5-orders guard is too low. During slow but not zero-traffic periods, a single cancellation out of 6-8 orders triggers Warning. Recommend raising to 15 orders minimum for Warning tier, keeping 5 for Info tier.
For an API gateway serving all mobile app traffic, 15% error rate is already catastrophic — 1 in 7 requests failing. The report's 20% suggestion was overly conservative.

Proposed batch window (04:30-06:30) doesn't overlap with existing off-hours mute (07:00-12:00). Between 06:30-07:00 UTC, a late-running batch job would trigger alerts. Consider extending batch window to 07:00 UTC to merge cleanly.
